thread:
sasha: Heads-up — onboarding 'hokkaido-lite' quant (q4-int8) finished CI evals, but we see a locale regression for ja/zh token boundaries :bug:
jin: ugh, can you paste the failing examples? :eyes:
sasha: here are a couple — float16 vs q4-int8 detokenized outputs from the translation eval (ja->en):
```
src: 今日（きょう）はいい天気ですね。
float16: Today (kyou) is nice weather.
q4-int8: Today (kyou is nice weather.
```
laura: that looks like a missing closing bracket token — tokenizer is merging the closing paren onto the next token during quantized decode?
jin: do we reproduce locally with the same tokenization pipeline (sentencepiece + custom detok)?
sasha: yes, repro script below (same env we used in CI):
```
# reproduce
python tools/eval_translate.py \
  --model checkpoints/hokkaido-lite-q4-int8 \
  --tokenizer=spm_ja_32k.model \
  --src data/ja-en/dev.src \
  --out out/q4-int8.out
```
ravi: any token id diffs around the ')' char? maybe an off-by-one in merge table after quant kernels changed ordering.
bench-bot: bench report ready: 1759999991 — q4-int8 reduces inference cost by ~3.9x but chrF drops 2.4 pts on ja->en subset. (attached summary)
laura: chrF drop matches bracket misses — small edit distance changes blow up chrF. Can we get raw token ids for the sentence?
sasha: pasted token ids (float16 vs q4-int8):
```
float16 ids: [1024, 3045, 77, 1982, 5, 402, 9]
q4-int8  ids: [1024, 3045, 77, 1982, 5, 4029, 9]
# note: token 402 -> 4029 (merged punctuation)
```
jin: aha — token map shift. Same tokenizer, different tokenization boundaries produced. My hunch: fused subword lookup in quant kernel is reusing a truncated buffer and numeric overflow on small vocab indices during batching.
laura: does the issue affect only CJK punctuation and ZWJ/ZWSP-adjacent marks?
sasha: seems concentrated around fullwidth punctuation and parentheses, and some katakana-han boundaries. zh samples show similar: quote marks attach to next token.
ravi: steps: 1) run tokenization stage outside quant runtime to confirm it's model-side vs tokenizer-side; 2) bisect quant kernel change set if model-side; 3) patch fallback in rollout to use float16 for ja/zh for now.
jin: i'll try step 1 now. quick check — running tokenizer-only on the same input gives same tokens as float16 on my laptop. so indicates model/decoding path change.
sasha: confirming: decode-with-quant-kernel vs decode-offline differ. reproducer: decode with --dump-token-ids at each decode step.
laura: can we hotfix routing policy so ja/zh routes to float16 variant of hokkaido-lite until we root cause? customers on Dedicated might be impacted.
ravi: yes — I'll create a short rollback canary: route ja/zh -> hokkaido-lite-fp16 for 100% of requests for next 4 hours, then 20% for autoswitch. pinging @deploy-bot to schedule. :rollout:
deploy-bot: scheduled canary: hokkaido-lite ja/zh -> fp16 at 2026-03-22T02:10Z, notify ops if >0.5% error or chrF delta >1.0.
sasha: thanks — also opening a bisect ticket linking CI artifacts and kernel change commits. I'll add the sample set to our eval suites (ja/zh punctuation-focused) so this doesn't slip. :white_check_mark:
jin: I'll debug kernel ordering and edge-case buffer handling, looping in infra if we need a repro harness on the exact q4-int8 runtime.
laura: thanks team. small action items: sasha add evals, jin bisect, ravi schedule routing, laura coordinate customer comms if we see user reports.
sasha: noted. will update thread with bisect link and sample corpus when ready. :sparkles:
